q: 1. Which one of the following is a component of a shield for tunnelling?
explain: A tunnelling shield's essential components include the cutting edge (which advances into the ground ahead of excavation), along with the hood and tail, distinguishing it from liner plates or trench jacks.

q: 2. Which one of the following statements is not correct for heading and benching method of tunnelling?
options: Drilling and mucking can be done simultaneously
Benching provides a plateform for working on heading
Removal of muck from the heading is very easy
explain: In the heading and benching method, mucking (removing debris) from the elevated heading portion is actually difficult (not easy) because of restricted working space and the need to lower material down, making this statement incorrect.

q: 3. In case of drift method of tunnelling, the drift may be excavated at
explain: The pilot drift (small preliminary tunnel) in the drift method can be excavated at the centre, top (crown), or bottom (invert) of the section depending on ground conditions, so all locations are valid options.

q: 4. Pick up the correct statement from the following during tunnel excavation
options: Oxygen should not be less than 19.5%
Carbondioxide should not be more than 0.5%
Hydrogen sulphide should not be more than 0.001%
explain: All these are recognized safe air-quality limits (oxygen minimum, CO2 maximum, H2S maximum) mandated for worker safety during tunnel excavation.

q: 5. The most commonly adopted pattern of cut holes is
explain: Various cut-hole patterns — horizontal wedge, pyramid, fan, and V-cut — are all commonly used in tunnel blasting, chosen based on rock type and tunnel section.

q: 6. Which one of the following linings is suitable for shield driven tunnels particularly in the subaqueous regions :
explain: Cast iron segmental lining is preferred for shield-driven tunnels beneath water bodies (subaqueous) because it provides high strength and excellent watertightness against high external water pressure.

q: 7. Pick up the mechanical ventilation method used for tunnels from the following
options: blowing fresh air by ducts to the face of tunnel
exhausting foul air by ducts from the face of the tunnel and permitting fresh air through the tunnel
blowing fresh air and exhausting foul air by ducts
explain: Mechanical tunnel ventilation can use blowing (supply), exhausting (extraction), or combined blowing-and-exhausting systems — all are recognized ventilation strategies.

q: 8. For highways, tunnelling is preferred to if the open cut exceeds :
explain: For highway alignments, tunnelling becomes economically preferable over deep open cutting once the cut depth exceeds about 15 m (theoretically up to about 18 m), beyond which cutting costs escalate.

q: 9. Which one of the following statements is not correct in respect of setting of an inclined tunnel:
options: Reference points are constructed on the roof of tunnels
The alignment is fixed from upper/lower apex point.
The level of the invert at the heading is marked by a tape.
explain: According to the book's answer key, all three statements about setting out an inclined tunnel (roof reference points, apex-based alignment, invert level marking) are correct, so 'none of the above' is the right choice.

q: 10. Concrete lining is provided concurrently with the driving operation in case of
explain: In hard/rock terrain, concrete lining can be placed concurrently with excavation advance since the rock itself is stable enough to remain open temporarily without immediate support.

q: 11. Which one of the following statements is not correct with regard to heading and benching method of tunnelling.
options: Driving of tunnel is done in two portions of its section
Driving the top portion is done in advance of the bottom portion
After driving the top portion 3 m to 3.5 m holes are drilled into the head and bench
Firing of head holes is done just before the bench holes are fired
explain: In practice, the bench holes are fired first (or with adequate free face preparation), and head holes are fired appropriately timed relative to that — not simply 'just before' as stated, making this the incorrect statement.

q: 12. Which one of the following methods is generally used for the layout of the muck-car tracks
options: the cherry picker, California crossing, Dixon conveyor
explain: Multiple layout methods (grasshopper, passing track, cherry picker/California crossing, Dixon conveyor) are all recognized techniques for arranging muck-car tracks in tunnel construction.

q: 13. In the wooded bulk-head, used for mucking in steep grade tunnels,
explain: A wooden bulkhead used for controlling muck flow in steep-grade tunnels is typically constructed with two openings to manage material discharge.

q: 14. An overhead track on a large truss frame is required in case of car changer by
explain: The grasshopper method for muck-car changing uses an overhead track supported on a large truss frame to shift empty/loaded cars past each other.

q: 15. For hauling muck from the tunnel, the following type of muck-car is used
explain: Various muck-car types (muck box, ballast-ship type, side dump, U-bottom cars) are all used in practice for hauling excavated material out of a tunnel.

q: 16. Which one of the following methods is adopted for permanent drainage of tunnels :
explain: Permanent tunnel drainage relies on a combination of longitudinal drains, continuous open drains, and impermeable concrete lining with grouting — all methods work together for long-term water management.

q: 17. Pick the tunnel which is not a sub-group of traffic tunnels.
explain: Sewage tunnels fall under public utility tunnels (for conveying wastewater), not under traffic tunnels, which cover railway, highway, and pedestrian passages.

q: 18. Tunnels associated with hydropower generation are called
explain: Tunnels built specifically to convey water for electricity generation at hydroelectric projects are termed hydropower tunnels.

q: 19. Circular section of tunnels is not suitable for
explain: A circular section, while structurally efficient for water conveyance and shield-driven tunnels in loose ground, is comparatively less convenient for placing/forming concrete lining uniformly compared to other shapes.

q: 20. A good blast with a good yield is obtained if the cut hole is
explain: Cut holes angled at about 45° to the tunnel face create an effective wedge/relief for the main blast, producing a good yield compared to holes drilled normal to the face.

q: 21. In 'N' is the number of shafts used, then the total number of faces available for attacking the excavation and construction in tunnels are
explain: Each shaft provides two working faces (one in each direction along the tunnel), plus the two natural end faces (portals) of the tunnel, giving a total of 2N+2 faces.

q: 22. If 'D' is the diameter of tunnel in meters then the thickness of lining in mm, as pe the empirical formula is given by
explain: A commonly cited empirical formula for tunnel lining thickness (in mm) is approximately t = 82D, where D is the tunnel diameter in metres.

q: 23. The most suitable soil for compresses air tunneling is
explain: Compressed air tunnelling works best in soft, saturated clay and silty ground because the applied air pressure effectively balances groundwater pressure and stabilizes the face, unlike highly permeable sand/gravel where air would simply escape.

q: 24. The most suitable soil for compressed air tunneling is .............
explain: Per the reference key, silt is marked as most suitable for compressed air tunneling in this classification.

q: 25. The entrance of tunnel is called .............
explain: The entrance/opening of a tunnel is termed the portal.

q: 26. Drift method of tunneling is used to construct tunnels in .............
explain: The drift method, involving excavation of a small pilot tunnel first, is typically used in rock formations.

q: 27. In full face method of constructing tunnels, the first operation relates to .............
options: excavation of one drift in the center
excavation being done along the periphery
explain: The full face method begins with excavating a central pilot drift, which is then enlarged outward to the full tunnel section.

q: 28. Which one of the following is a component of a shield for tunneling?
explain: The cutting edge is a key structural component of a tunneling shield, used to cut into the ground as the shield advances.

q: 29. In Belgium method of tunneling .............
options: construction of side walls is completed before invert and roof arch are built
construction of roof arch is completed before side walls and invert are built
construction of invert is completed before side walls and roof arch are built
construction of invert and side walls is completed before roof arch is built
explain: In the Belgian method, the roof arch is constructed first, providing support before the side walls and invert are excavated and built below.

q: 30. A good blast with a good yield is obtained if the cut hole is .............
explain: A shallow-angled cut hole (around 15° to the face) is used to create an effective free face for a good blasting yield.

q: 31. Ribs are used for strengthening and stiffening the liner plate for tunnels of diameter greater than .............
explain: For tunnels with diameter greater than about 3 m, additional steel ribs are used to reinforce and stiffen the liner plates.

q: 32. As compared to a single free face, if a charge of explosive is placed equidistant from two faces, then the yield .............
explain: A charge placed between two free faces benefits from reduced resistance on both sides, increasing blast yield by roughly 2.25 times compared to a single free face.
